metadata.title: NexusMED Antibacterial Dosing Engine V3 - Evidence Verified Core
metadata.evidence_scope: Adult hospital/ICU antibacterial dosing core. Pediatric dosing is out of scope for this V3 unless explicitly present in a label; do not infer.
metadata.verification_method: Current FDA/DailyMed official labeling + IDSA 2026 AMR guidance + CLSI M100 Ed36 + EUCAST v16.1 + high-level PubMed consensus/meta-analysis for PK/PD/TDM.
metadata.important_disclaimer: Clinical decision support dataset, not autonomous prescribing. Rules require local formulary, microbiology standard, patient-specific validation and clinician oversight.
metadata.sanford_note: Sanford Guide was NOT used as an unseen source because no licensed Sanford dataset was directly accessible in this session. Do not claim Sanford cross-validation unless Nexus has a licensed integration.
metadata.source_policy: No Wikipedia, blogs, commercial SEO dosing pages, or unsourced web pages are accepted as source-of-truth.

engine_rules.text: Store FDA/label dosing and guideline/PK-PD dosing in separate fields. If they differ, display both with context; never silently overwrite.
Use the renal estimator specified by the source/label (e.g., Cockcroft-Gault CrCl vs eGFR). Never silently substitute one estimator for another.
If renal function is rapidly changing, do not auto-maintain from a single steady-state CrCl. Flag frequent reassessment and TDM when available.
Before any RRT dose: require IHD vs SLED/PIRRT vs CVVH/CVVHD/CVVHDF, effective effluent, downtime, residual urine/renal function and timing relative to dialysis.
Never use the CrCl <10 regimen as a surrogate for CRRT. Use agent-specific CRRT evidence only; otherwise SPECIALIST_REVIEW.
Screen critically ill patients for augmented renal clearance. CrCl >=130 mL/min is a common ARC threshold, but drug-specific thresholds take priority (e.g., cefiderocol >=120).
In critically ill adults with sepsis/septic shock, prolonged beta-lactam infusion is supported by randomized-trial meta-analysis; use drug stability/compatibility and a validated regimen.
AST interpretation must be versioned separately (CLSI M100 Ed36 2026 or EUCAST v16.1 2026). Do not mix breakpoint standards inside one result.
Dose selection is not susceptibility interpretation. Require organism, site, MIC/AST method and selected breakpoint standard before MIC-based claims.
For mg/kg dosing require documented weight and drug-specific scalar (TBW/IBW/AdjBW/LBW). Block lb interpreted as kg.
For vancomycin and repeated aminoglycoside therapy, TDM is part of the dosing rule, not optional metadata.
LLM may interpret clinical context but must not generate a dose absent an executable verified rule. Missing rule -> SPECIALIST_REVIEW, not a guessed number.
